To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
linseed fatty acids can reduce methane production from dairy cows, and the form of presentation of these fatty acids has an impact on methane production.
linseed fatty acids are a promising means of reducing methane emissions from dairy cows, but the form of presentation greatly influences the magnitude of the response.

feeding crude linseed (5.7%) and extruded linseed to dairy cows decreased methane output (-12 and -38%, respectively) and that feeding linseed oil (5.7%, as a replacement for 5.7% fat) decreased methane output (-64%) compared with a control diet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of feeding dairy cows different forms of linseed on methane output, total tract digestibilities, and performance.
the development of a new feed additive for dairy cows to reduce methane emissions and improve milk production.
developing strategies to reduce methane production in ruminants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
feeding linseed FA to dairy cows decreases methane output and that this effect depends on the form of presentation of these FA.
feeding linseed oil to dairy cows is a very efficient method of reducing CH4 production, but the effect of this oil on the performance of the cows must be taken into account.

feeding dairy cows linseed in a form that does not alter ruminal fermentation (e.g., CLS) has no impact on methane output and milk production, but that feeding linseed in a way that alters ruminal fermentation (ELS and LSO) decreases methane output at the expense of milk production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the form of presentation of dietary linseed fatty acid has an impact on methane output from dairy cattle.
feeding dairy cows linseed oil, extruded linseeds, or crude linseeds reduced methane emissions, but the form of presentation of the oil had a large effect on methane output.
the form in which linseed FA are fed to dairy cows greatly influences the efficiency of their utilization and the extent of their effects on ruminal methane output and milk production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the form of presentation of the linseed FA greatly influenced CH(4) emission, with extruded linseed and linseed oil being more effective than the crude product.
methane output from dairy cow can be reduced by dietary linseed FA.
linseed oil is the most promising form to be used in the diet to mitigate methane emissions in ruminants, with a reduction of 38% of methane production per kilogram of feed.
